items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: and later that year you also recorded with Mez Mezro and his orchestra.

ctx.x: . . . and talk about . . . oh, before we do that, we’re still working with 1933 and your recordings, and it struck me, we mentioned there was one integrated session of the Chocolate Dandies with that title—anachronistic title, oddly enough; it was an integrated band—and later that year you also recorded with Mez Mezro and his orchestra. I believe that was an offshoot of some grandiose idea he had to tour with an interracial group, which never came to fruition, but this was sort of a spin-off from that. Then you…
[unclear], was that one of the songs?

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: No, that's what I might call an interesting anecdote, but I don't remember it.

ctx.x: Another thing, around that time. There's a -- in a discussion with Bud Freeman, that was not Bud Freeman, although he was involved -- it was Mezz Mezzrow, Mezzra -- Mezzra, in his book, 'Really the BLues' mentions that you helped him with what he calls the first interracial band; everybody's got the first interracial band -- he had it in 1933.
He says in August of 1933 he signed a contract with a financial backer to support a mixed Big Band, which had Alex Hill, as the arranger, to front it. This is in Mezzrow's Mezra's book.
